import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I moved "Is this a good idea?" up to sit right after the bottom line, since it's the question you asked first. The lead's note on how the report was produced now opens the Sources section. The rest keeps the lead's order and wording, and a script check confirmed that every changed line was an intended edit. Changes beyond that:
- **Headings:** to make four headings safe link targets, I moved their parenthetical or after-colon text into the section's first line: "Vault evidence", "Adjustments to the brief", "Key grammar", and "Making the existing tie obvious".
- **Links:** I added a few links within the document: from the bottom line to the evidence, the adjustments and the design; from the "§ Key grammar" mention; from the `bob.md` case; and from the recommended solution to the key grammar and the tie badges.

**Diagrams:** both proposed diagrams are placed, each copied exactly and wrapped in its figure anchor:
- `release-confirmation` → `#figure-release-confirmation`, at the end of the "Why the confirm asymmetry" paragraph.
- `cross-note-failures` → `#figure-cross-note-failures`, after the "Reliability and write order" list.

None were left out. The lead's own state diagram (the `tie-states.png` image plus its Mermaid version) is unchanged, so the file has three Mermaid diagrams: the lead's one plus the two new ones. Two grk images were also registered (`pair-states.png`, `links-gestures.png`), but the lead's report only mentions their folder and doesn't embed them, so I didn't add them.

**Checks:**
- **Links:** both relative image links resolve, and every in-document and figure link matches an anchor in `pandoc -t html`. The report has no external URLs, so no link was unverifiable or dropped.
- **Content:** every table cell and code block from the lead's report is in the new file.
- **Manifest:** the diagram manifest's `diagrams:` label wouldn't resolve (`unknown_kind`), so I read it through its file reference instead. Its source matches the lead's report.
